clue.text: Electronics firm covers writer's trading benefits

indicators.note: the firm's name wraps around the writer's words, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Sony is the Japanese electronics company
the writer is the setter, so 'writer's' stands for 'I am', shortened to I'M

explanation.surface: A tech company seems to shield an author's commercial perks.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'benefits' here are church benefices, not employee perks.
explanation.definitionFit: Simony is the buying and selling of church offices, or benefices, so it is trade in ecclesiastical livings.

clue.text: Bad language is ultimately tiresome

indicators.note: ultimately picks the very last letter of the word is

parts.note: wearing means tiresome or exhausting

explanation.surface: Foul words are, in the end, tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: S, the end of 'is', comes before WEARING.
explanation.definitionFit: Swearing is the use of profanity, crude or offensive words.

clue.text: Placated girl with hood, one left out of ground

parts.note: a moll is a gangster's girlfriend, the girl who goes with a hood, or hoodlum
one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: out of tells us the letter for left is taken away from the ground's word

parts.note: a field is a sports ground

explanation.surface: A soothed girl in a hood was left out of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hood' looks like a garment but is a hoodlum. 'left out of' removes L from FIELD, giving FIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Mollified means calmed or soothed, so pacified, the same as placated.

clue.text: Perhaps Hazel and Margaret do what dribblers do

parts.note: a hazel is an example of a nut tree, hence perhaps
Meg is a short form of Margaret

explanation.surface: Two women, Hazel and Margaret, seem to be dribbling.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazel and Margaret look like two women; only Margaret is. In football, to nutmeg is to play the ball between an opponent's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Footballers dribbling past a defender may slip the ball through their legs, a trick called a nutmeg.

clue.text: Workers block a rear pier

indicators.note: the workers stand in the middle of the other letters, blocking them like an obstruction

parts.note: a butt is a person's rear
workers are men in crossword shorthand

explanation.surface: Labourers obstruct a pier at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: An abutment is a supporting structure, such as the pier at the end of a bridge that takes the thrust of an arch.

clue.text: Bitterly disappointed but apparently OK

parts.note: the middle, or heart, of the word broken is the pair of letters O and K, so the clue's OK is what the answer describes

explanation.surface: Deeply upset but outwardly fine.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, the heart of BROKEN, and it gives OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone heartbroken is overwhelmed by grief or disappointment, the state of a crushed spirit.

clue.text: Proclaim bottom end of page in Times

indicators.note: in places the bottom and the page's last letter within the two time letters

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so two times are TT
a rump is a bottom

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of page

explanation.surface: Announce the foot of a page in the Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is two T's; RUMP and E go between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to announce it loudly and widely, as if with a fanfare.

clue.text: Surrealist stumped European sailors first

indicators.note: first says the European and the sailors come before the stumped letters

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
st is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: A Surrealist painter was baffled by European seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter can be out stumped, written st on the scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German painter who was a leading figure of Dada and Surrealism.

clue.text: Your old group put up hoarding in sea once

indicators.note: the group's letters store the old word for your inside them, as a hoard is kept
in a down entry put up means the group word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a set is a group
thy is the archaic word for your

explanation.surface: Your former band raised a billboard in an ancient ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoarding' looks like a billboard but means storing. 'put up' turns SET into TES, which holds THY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethys is the name geologists give to an ancient ocean that once lay between the supercontinents Gondwana and Laurasia.

clue.text: Back story involving college's flair

indicators.note: the turned-round story takes in the college letter, wrapping it inside
back tells us to read the word for story from end to start

parts.note: a tale is a story
C is a standard abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A reversed tale includes a university's style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns TALE into ELAT, and C goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant success or showy panache, a close match for stylish flair.

clue.text: Mystery doctor approaches horse with dope

parts.note: Doctor Who, the BBC time traveller, gives WHO
a dun is a greyish-brown horse
a nit is a dope, a fool

explanation.surface: A physician walks up to a horse carrying drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like a drug for doping the horse, but it means an idiot. Doctor Who is a long-running British science-fiction television series.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunnit is a detective story, a mystery in which the reader guesses the culprit.

clue.text: It stops scaling tree after snow flurries

indicators.note: flurries suggests letters whirled about like snow, so tree after snow is rearranged

explanation.surface: A climber stops scaling a tree as snow flurries begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scaling' suggests climbing, but it means limescale build-up. 'flurries' rearranges TREE AFTER SNOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that removes calcium and magnesium from hard water prevents limescale forming in pipes and kettles.

clue.text: Clothing torn catching train

indicators.note: the word for torn holds the word for train inside it, as if caught

parts.note: rent is an old past participle of rend, meaning torn
to train a gun is to aim it

explanation.surface: Garments ripped while boarding a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway train, but it means to aim, as with a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is a literary word for garments or attire.

clue.text: Understanding English writer's engaging way

indicators.note: the writer's word engages, or holds, the word for way within it

parts.note: the writer is the setter, so 'writer's' means 'my'
a path is a way

explanation.surface: Comprehension of an English author's charming manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Empathy is the capacity to share and comprehend another person's feelings, a kind of understanding.

clue.text: PIN number trouble

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Problems with one's bank card code.
explanation.walkthrough: PIN in capitals suggests a personal identification number, but it is just a pin, a fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail and a pin are both slender metal fasteners hammered or pushed in to hold things.

clue.text: Problem for privates — pert girl is after other ones

indicators.note: the girl and 'is' come after the other ones, so they follow in the answer

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, the soldiers who are not officers, so 'other ones' is a playful pointer
a chit is a cheeky or impudent young girl

explanation.surface: A soldier's trouble: a cheeky girl pursuing other men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Privates' hints at army privates, tying in with OR (other ranks), but means the private parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchitis is inflammation of the testicles, a medical complaint affecting the genitals.

clue.text: Golf interrupting calm — it upset African sanctuary

indicators.note: the golf letter breaks into the calm word, sitting inside it

parts.note: serene means calm
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means the word it is turned upside down, read in reverse

explanation.surface: A round of golf disturbs the peace of an African wildlife park.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes into SERENE, and 'upset' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast national park in Tanzania famous for wildlife migrations, a protected reserve.

clue.text: One forgets amateur cinema's developed

indicators.note: developed, as with film, suggests the letters are processed into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone forgets what the amateur film club has developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges the letters of CINEMA'S, ignoring the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesiac is a person suffering memory loss, someone who cannot remember.

clue.text: Papers back plan to nail mother, one in embassy

indicators.note: back says the papers' abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: ID stands for identity papers

indicators.note: the plan nails, or holds fast, the mother inside it

parts.note: a plot is a plan
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Documents expose a scheme to trap a mother, involving someone at an embassy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to nail' looks like a verb about catching a mother, but it signals one piece holding another.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat is an official representing a country abroad, typically based at an embassy.

clue.text: Old man's son dismissed issue

parts.note: the old man is pa, a father, so old man's is PA'S
a batter who is dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A father's son was sent away from a family matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like offspring, which fits the son, but it is a verb meaning to hand out.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass out leaflets or supplies is to distribute them, the sense of issue as giving out.

clue.text: Transport first of modern paintings around

indicators.note: around turns the word for paintings round to face the other way

parts.note: paintings are art

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of modern

explanation.surface: Moving the earliest modern pictures about.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a passenger vehicle running on rails along streets, a form of public transport.

clue.text: Ridiculous American got up in an inferior way

indicators.note: in places the turned American letters inside the other pieces

parts.note: B is second-rate, as in a B-movie
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

indicators.note: in a down entry got up means the American letters rise, read bottom to top

parts.note: US means American

explanation.surface: A ridiculous American dressed up in an inferior manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' looks like dressed, but in a down clue it lifts the American letters to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absurd is wildly unreasonable or laughable, the same as ridiculous.

clue.text: Round trip in Ford that's exchanged in Prague

indicators.note: in places the round and trip pieces within the car's name

parts.note: the Ka is a small Ford car
a round shape is O
a run is a short trip

explanation.surface: A circular drive in a Ford Ka around a Czech city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ka was a small Ford hatchback sold in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The koruna is the Czech currency, the money used and changed in the Czech capital.

clue.text: Watch kids gorge nonstop during scrap

indicators.note: the shortened gorge happens during the scrap, sitting inside its letters

parts.note: a bit is a scrap

indicators.note: nonstop means the gorge loses its final stop, the closing letter

parts.note: an abyss is a deep gorge

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on children eating continuously during a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gorge' looks like a verb for eating greedily but is a chasm; 'scrap' seems a fight but is a small piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To babysit is to look after children while their parents are out, minding the young ones.

clue.text: Fight fine Scottish Liberal

parts.note: braw is Scots for fine or good

explanation.surface: A fight over fines for a Scottish Liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like a penalty but is an adjective, braw in Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a rough, noisy fight or scuffle.

clue.text: Thump counter furiously

indicators.note: furiously suggests the letters of counter thrashed around into a new order

explanation.surface: Bang angrily on a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furiously' rearranges COUNTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to beat or defeat heavily, so it can mean to thrash or hit hard.

clue.text: Peacekeepers loved patrolling northern plain

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: the loved word goes around the northern letter, like guards circling an area

parts.note: adored means loved

explanation.surface: Popular UN troops guard a northern flatland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like a flat landscape but is an adjective meaning simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Unadorned means without decoration, so something left plain and simple.

clue.text: Our earliest homes found in the outer islands

indicators.note: found in says the letters are tucked away inside the words outer islands

explanation.surface: Ancestral settlements discovered on remote islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our earliest homes' suggests ancient dwellings, but means the wombs we lived in before birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Each person's first dwelling is the womb, the organ in which a foetus grows, so wombs are our first homes.

clue.text: Time-wasting form of idolatry

indicators.note: a form of the word idolatry means its letters reshaped into another order

explanation.surface: Worshipping idols is a waste of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges IDOLATRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory describes someone slow or tending to delay, so dawdling and wasting time.

clue.text: PC arrests a Northern Irish nutter

indicators.note: the computer holds the other letters inside, as a police officer holds a suspect

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple personal computer
NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland or Northern Irish

explanation.surface: A police constable detains a crazy man from Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a police constable, which 'arrests' backs up, but it is a personal computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutter is British slang for a crazy person, a madman or lunatic.
